# flightdeck_service_account (Resource)

Manages a Flightdeck service account: a login for an application or a bot, not a person. Give it access to a project with `flightdeck_project_member`, using this resource's `id` as `user_id`, and give the application a token with `flightdeck_service_account_api_token`.

**Every read and write needs a token whose user is a workspace owner or admin.**

`email_address` names the account and can't be changed, so a new address replaces it. Flightdeck stores addresses in lower case, so write it in lower case, with no spaces at either end. An address that belongs to a person is refused. So is one that is already a service account in this workspace, and the error gives the id to import it with.

`name` defaults to the part of the address before the `@`. **A service account can be in more than one workspace, and its name is the same in all of them.** If the address belongs to a service account that is already in another workspace, creating this resource adds that account to this workspace with the name it already has, and Flightdeck won't rename it while it is in the other workspace. So if `name` is set to something else, the apply fails, takes the account back out of this workspace, and names the name to use. A later rename is refused the same way. An account that was removed from every workspace comes back with the configured `name`, or the name it had when `name` is left out.

Deleting the resource removes the account from this workspace only, along with its API tokens and project memberships here. Flightdeck never deletes the account itself, so creating it again with the same address brings back the same `id`.

A create carries an idempotency key built from `email_address` and `name`, so a create retried after a lost response doesn't fail. Flightdeck keeps those keys per provider token. So two resources with the same address and name, created with the same provider token within 24 hours of each other, are one create: both manage one account, and destroying either removes it. Created with different provider tokens, the second create is refused because the address is already a service account in this workspace, and the error gives the id to import.

Import by numeric id: `terraform import flightdeck_service_account.deploy 980190966`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "flightdeck_project" "app" {
  name       = "Mobile App"
  identifier = "APP"
}

# A login for the application, not a person. Write the address in lower
# case: Flightdeck stores it that way.
resource "flightdeck_service_account" "deploy" {
  email_address = "deploy-bot@machineusers.example.com"
  name          = "Deploy Bot"
}

# Give it only the project it works in. user_id takes the service account's id.
resource "flightdeck_project_member" "deploy" {
  project_id = flightdeck_project.app.id
  user_id    = flightdeck_service_account.deploy.id
  role       = "member"
}

# The token the application calls Flightdeck's API with.
resource "flightdeck_service_account_api_token" "deploy" {
  service_account_id = flightdeck_service_account.deploy.id
  name               = "Deploy production"
  expires_at         = "2027-06-01T00:00:00Z"
}

# The token value is only returned on create; hand it to the application
# through a secret store rather than an output.
# output "deploy_token" {
#   value     = flightdeck_service_account_api_token.deploy.token
#   sensitive = true
# }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email_address` (String) The account's email address. It only names the account, so it need not reach a real inbox, but it must have one `@` and no spaces. Write it in lower case. At most 255 characters. Changing it replaces the account.

### Optional

- `name` (String) Display name, at most 255 characters. Leave it out to use the part of the address before the `@`, or the name the account already has when Flightdeck already has one with this address. Removing it keeps the current name. The name can't be changed while the account is also in another workspace, so then it must be the name the account has, or left out.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) Numeric id of the service account. It is the account's user id, so it is what `flightdeck_project_member.user_id` takes.
- `joined_at` (String) When the account joined this workspace (RFC 3339, in the server's time zone).
- `role` (String) The account's workspace role. A service account is always a `member`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the service account's numeric id, which is its user id (the one
# flightdeck_project_member.user_id takes).
terraform import flightdeck_service_account.deploy 980190966
```
